_exec_summary.SummaryText:
The accidental release prevention and emergency response policies at the stationary source [40 CFR 68.155(a)]:
The Abad Foam Waco, TX facility is a toluene diisocyanate (TDI) foam pouring facility, utilizing TDI and polyol to produce polyurethane foam products. The facility is a non-responding site and has coordinated with the local Waco Fire Department to respond in the case of accidental release or fire/explosion. They have also coordinated with the local McLennan County LEPC.
The stationary source and regulated substances handled [40 CFR 68.155(b)]:
The Abad Foam Waco, TX facility has two storage vessels that are loaded with TDI once a month. There are no outlets or inlets to the atmosphere fitted on the two vessels, except for emergency pressure release valves that only open to prevent catastrophic failure. Based on the EPA RMP regulation, this facility is subject to RMP regulation due to handling and transfer of TDI above the threshold quantity of 10,000 lbs. 

The general accidental release prevention program and chemical-specific prevention steps [40 CFR 68.155(c)]:
Process Safety Information [40 CFR Part 68.65]
Abad Foam maintains a detailed record of safety information that describes the chemical hazards, operating parameters, and equipment design and details associated with the TDI loading and foam pouring processes. 

Process Hazard Analysis [40 CFR Part 68.67]
Abad Foam conducts process hazard analyses as necessary to ensure that hazards associated with their foam pouring process are identified and controlled effectively. HAZOP methodology used to carry out these analyses, but other methods may be used at the discretion of the process hazard analysis team. Teams are comprised of qualified personnel with expertise in the process and operations of the facility, and studies are re-evaluated every five (5) years at minimum.

Written Operating Procedures [40 CFR Part 68.69]
Detailed written operating procedures are maintained for TDI loading and foam pouring

processing. Step-by-step instructions are given with special safety precautions highlighted. All operations are ceased in the event that any unsafe conditions should arise. Additionally, training is provided for operators and maintenance personnel. This supplements the existing contractor training programs. 

Employee Training [40 CFR Part 68.71]
Abad Foam has a training program in place to ensure all authorized employees and contractors who are working in the TDI foam pouring process are competent in all relevant operating procedures. 

Mechanical Integrity [40 CFR Part 68.73]
The equipment and piping systems at the Abad Foam Waco, TX location are routinely inspected to determine the wall thicknesses at critical points of the piping. This program provides assurance that equipment and piping failure will not occur due to localized corrosion. Records of all inspections are maintained by Abad Foam. 

Management of Change [MOC] [40 CFR Part 68.75]
Written procedures are in place to manage potential changes in the TDI foam pouring processs procedures, equipment, or technology. Authorized employees whose jobs tasks are affected by a potential modification are promptly informed of and trained on the changes and their implications.

Pre-Startup Safety Review [PSSR] [40 CFR Part 68.77]
Pre-startup safety reviews are conducted after any change to the TDI foam pouring systems procedures, equipment, or technology are implemented. These reviews are conducted to confirm that conditions and procedures are suitable for safe startup prior to placing the system into operation.

Compliance Audits [40 CFR Part 68.79]
Abad Foam conducts PSM/RMP audits every three (3) years at minimum in order to determine whether the provisions set under the RMP rule are being effectively implemented. Any corrective actions required as a result of these audits will be completed in a safe and timely manner. 

Incident Investigation [40 CFR Part 68.81]
Abad Foam promptly investigates any incident that

has resulted in, or could have reasonably resulted in, an unintentional release of TDI. These investigations are undertaken within 48 hours of the incident to identify the situation leading to the event, as well as to define any corrective actions implemented to prevent the release from reoccurring. All reports are maintained onsite for a minimum of five (5) years. 

Employee Participation [40 CFR Part 68.83]
The Abad Foam Waco, TX facility has written policies in addition aimed at preventing the release of TDI. Each employee must review these policies at least annually.  

Hot Work Permit [40 CFR Part 68.85]
Abad Foam requires issuance of a hot work permit for hot work operations conducted on or near the covered process.

Contractor Safety Program [40 CFR Part 68.87] 
Abad Foam may hire contractors to conduct specialized maintenance and/or construction activities, among other specialized activities, related to the foam pouring process. Prior to selecting a contractor, Abad Foam conducts an evaluation of the potential contractors safety performance initially and annually thereafter. Abad Foam will inform contractors of known potential hazards relating to their work with TDI. Contractors are also informed of emergency response procedures in the case of an accidental release of TDI.
The five-year accident history [40 CFR 68.155(d)]:
The Abad Foam Waco, TX facility has not had any accidents within the past five years that require reporting.

The emergency response program [40 CFR 68.155(e)]:
In the event of an incident, Abad Foam has an emergency action plan that personnel follow to evacuate to a safe location. The foam pouring process can be shut down on an emergency basis and the facility has a plan in place for evacuations and notification of local emergency response agencies. The facility is a non-responding facility and relies on the Waco Fire Department to respond to chemical releases. 

Planned changes to improve safety [40 CFR 68.155(f)]:
The Abad Foam Waco, T

X facility has implemented components of the Program Level 2 RMP, which ensures improved safety at the facility. Some of these components include employee safety training, management of change procedures, standard operating procedures, incident investigation procedures, and compliance audits. If it is determined that additional safety corrections are required, they will be implemented in a timely and efficient manner.
